authority: PROJECT_CONSTITUTION.md; S208 Board A Frozen Principles; CAQS_v1.0.md

summary: Framework v2 is sufficient for Part 2 expansion without architectural modification. The governance guard, identity model, pre-flight gates, delta review, scan-once pipeline, and traceability infrastructure are content-agnostic. Part 2 requires content, metadata extension, and quality-first authoring — not new architecture.

quality_first_authoring.key_question: Does Framework v2 ensure Part 2 content meets the same quality standards as Part 1?
quality_first_authoring.assessment: Yes. The CAQS §1.6 six-dimension verification standard is content-agnostic. All 6 dimensions (Correctness, Precision, Difficulty Calibration, Distractor Engineering, Blueprint Alignment, CMA Relevance) apply to Part 2 as they apply to Part 1. Only dimension 6 ('CMA Part 1 Relevance') needs modification to become 'CMA Part 2 Relevance' — a configuration change, not an architectural change.
evidence: CAQS §1.6 verifies correctness against authoritative standards — Part 2 standards (IFRS, strategic finance, risk management) are different content, same verification pattern
Pre-flight gates (Gates 0-4) auto-extend to any new pack file — structural scans are format-aware, not content-aware
Governance guard rules (1-6) are domain-agnostic — they check structural integrity, not accounting correctness
requirements: Extend CAQS dimension 6 from 'CMA Part 1 Relevance' to 'CMA Part Relevance (Part 1 or Part 2 as appropriate)'
Register Part 2-specific authoritative standards in the CAQS alignment requirements (§1.3)
Verify governance guard rules produce correct results on Part 2 pack files (same structural format expected)

analyze_evaluate_growth.key_question: Can Part 2 scale within Framework v2's batch infrastructure?
analyze_evaluate_growth.assessment: Yes. Framework v2's certification pipeline demonstrated 304.5 items/day throughput and 2,600 items/sec scan speed. The 30-item batch cap (Rule 5) and delta review (80% unchanged items skipped) apply identically to Part 2. The bottleneck is content authoring, not pipeline throughput.
evidence: Pipeline throughput: 2,600 items/sec (mean over 2 waves, S813 operational evidence)
Certification velocity: 304.5 items/day over 4 days, 30 cert events
Batch cap: ≤30 items per change-set (Rule 5) — applies to all packs regardless of Part
Delta review: 80% items unchanged between waves → only 20% re-reviewed — applies universally
requirements: Estimate Part 2 content volume to plan certification wave cadence
Establish Part 2 quality baseline before ramping certification velocity
Plan for potential governance guard regex extension for new pack filenames (pack_f_corrected.js etc.)

risks.mitigation: Pipeline scales linearly; 2,600 items/sec handles any reasonable volume
This is a human/content constraint, not architectural. Framework v2 does not control authoring throughput.

blueprint_expansion.key_question: Does Part 2 CSO map cleanly to Framework v2's metadata and identity infrastructure?
blueprint_expansion.assessment: Yes, with metadata extension. The QUESTION_METADATA_STANDARD.md must be extended for Part 2 domains, learning outcomes, and topic-authority mappings. The compound-key identity model (QID+CC+EW_Pattern+Template_Family+File_Path) naturally accommodates Part 2 QID prefixes. Separate pack files for Part 2 ensure no identity collision with Part 1.
evidence: Compound-key identity includes File_Path — Part 2 content in separate files is naturally disambiguated
BlueprintCoverageMatrix.csv extends with new rows per domain — existing domain structure (A-F) is arbitrary labels
S832 sectional coverage audit confirmed domain-level coverage metrics are label-agnostic
MASTER_QUESTION_REGISTRY.md auto-generation extends to any pack file with QuestionID markers
requirements: Extend QUESTION_METADATA_STANDARD.md with Part 2 domain identifiers, LO codes, and standard references
Extend BlueprintCoverageMatrix.csv with Part 2 domain rows
Define Part 2 QID naming convention (e.g., P2-A-001 through P2-F-XXX)
Register Part 2 pack files in governance guard source file regex (SOURCE_FILE_RE)
Update CAQS §1.3 alignment requirements for Part 2-specific standards

risks.mitigation: Scheduled before any Part 2 content authoring. 2-3 sessions estimated.

risks.risk: Governance guard regex may not match Part 2 pack filenames
risks.mitigation: Extend SOURCE_FILE_RE before Part 2 writes begin. Test with sample Part 2 pack file.

difficulty_calibration.key_question: Are DL-031 and DL-032 lessons applied to Part 2 difficulty calibration?
difficulty_calibration.assessment: Yes — the expansion rules (S208 Board C, rule P2-R5) explicitly prohibit template-assigned difficulty labels. Part 2 must use per-item cognitive assessment from first authoring. The DL-031 pattern (~500 definition-match items labeled Moderate that should be Easy) and DL-032 pattern (420 case items all labeled Moderate) are documented and must not recur.
evidence: DL-031 root cause: template rotation assigned difficulty by position (Easy, Moderate, Moderate, Difficult, Moderate) without cognitive assessment
DL-032 root cause: case authoring pipeline assigned Difficulty='Moderate' as default value with zero variance
S831 difficulty calibration recommendation: per-item Bloom's level + calculation complexity + distractor deceptiveness assessment
S208 Board C expansion rule P2-R5: template-assigned difficulty prohibited
requirements: Each Part 2 item must have independently assessed difficulty based on cognitive demand, not template position
Target CAQS §6.1 difficulty distribution for Part 2: Easy 15%, Moderate-Easy 20%, Moderate 30%, Difficult 25%, Very Difficult 10%
Target CAQS §6.2 Bloom's distribution: Remember 5%, Understand 15%, Apply 40%, Analyze 25%, Evaluate 15%
Difficulty calibration audit after first Part 2 certification wave to confirm distribution targets

risks.risk: As with Part 1, initial items may have inflated difficulty if template authoring is used
risks.mitigation: Expansion rule P2-R5 prohibits template authoring. First-wave audit catches any violations.

what_part2_requires: New pack files for Part 2 content (pack_f_corrected.js, pack_g_corrected.js etc.)
Quality-first authoring with CAQS §1.6 six-dimension verification
what_part2_does_not_require: New governance guard rules (existing rules are content-agnostic)
New identity model (compound key naturally extends to Part 2 QID prefixes)
New pre-flight gates (structural scans are format-aware, not content-aware)
New delta review architecture (SHA-256 hashing is content-agnostic)
New traceability infrastructure (registries extend to new pack files automatically)

recommendations.title: Define Part 2 QID naming convention before any content is authored
recommendations.description: Establish consistent QID format (e.g., P2-A-001 through P2-F-XXX) that integrates with existing compound-key identity model and governance guard regex.

recommendations.title: Extend governance guard file regex for Part 2 pack filenames
recommendations.description: Update SOURCE_FILE_RE in governance-guard.js to match Part 2 pack file naming pattern. Test with sample Part 2 pack file.

recommendations.title: Pilot Part 2 certification with 2-3 items to validate pipeline
recommendations.description: Author 2-3 sample Part 2 items and run through the full certification pipeline to confirm all gates, scans, and governance rules operate correctly on Part 2 content. Fix any issues before bulk authoring.
recommendations.target_session: After Part 2 standards registration, before bulk authoring

recommendations.title: Audit Part 1 difficulty calibration lessons before Part 2 authoring
recommendations.description: Review DL-031 (definition-match inflation) and DL-032 (uniform difficulty) as a pre-authoring lesson for Part 2 authors. Establish difficulty calibration training/briefing before authoring begins.

readiness_board_verdict: READY — Framework v2 is sufficient for Part 2. No architectural changes required. Standards extension and governance guard regex update are the only pre-authoring prerequisites.
